repo.description:
### Impact

A site with a wildcard iframe origin allowlist (e.g. `https://*.example.com`) could be tricked into embedding an iframe pointing to an attacker-controlled host. By inserting a URL authority separator before the allowed suffix, an attacker could cause the allowlist check to pass while the browser parses the iframe source as a different origin. The content rendered in the iframe would be attacker-controlled, independent of the allowlisted domain.

This affects:
- Sites using wildcard patterns in the `allowed_iframes` site setting (e.g. `https://*.typeform.com`)
- Onebox oEmbed responses, where the injected iframe would be rendered in posts created by users with posting privileges

Successful exploitation requires that a Discourse site has configured a wildcard pattern in their iframe allowlist, and that the attacker can create a post or otherwise trigger an oEmbed request for a URL they control.
repo.summary: Wildcard iframe origin allowlist bypass via authority separators
